# Tongjiang Lab

English | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

**Free, interactive 3D science lessons for high school — physics, chemistry, biology and geography.**

Try them online: **https://lab.tongjiang.app**

There are 54 lessons so far. Each one is a **single self-contained HTML file** of about 1 MB: double-click to open it, and it works offline, on a projector or on an interactive whiteboard. Every lesson is one 3D world with a live control console, a guiding question and a step-by-step path a teacher can follow from start to finish.

The lessons follow the Chinese national curriculum standards for senior high school and the People's Education Press (PEP) 2019 textbooks. The lesson interface is currently in Chinese; other languages are planned.

## How to use

- **Online**: click **▶ Open lesson** in the tables below. GitHub only shows the source code of an HTML file, so use these links to see the lessons.
- **Offline**: download all lessons as one zip from [Releases](https://github.com/smithjohn78390/tongjiang-lab/releases/latest), or download a single lesson from its page on https://lab.tongjiang.app, then open it in Chrome or Edge.
- **Embed**: `<iframe src="https://lab.tongjiang.app/<slug>" width="100%" style="aspect-ratio:16/9;border:0" allow="fullscreen"></iframe>`
- **Data**: [`catalog.json`](catalog.json) lists every lesson with its textbook location and steps.

items.readme:
watsonfind.icu: read it out loud. Watson, find. I see you.

--- ## What is Watson Watson is a **free OSINT search tool** (open-source intelligence) for Windows. It collects the trail a person leaves in public places — social networks, forums, games, developer sites — and turns it into a readable answer. Type a **nickname**, **email**, **phone number** or **website** and Watson checks **3,100+ public sources** for profiles and mentions. It's a digital footprint check, a username lookup and a social media search in one window — no terminal, no Python, no API keys. Use it to vet sellers before you pay, check a job offer, look at a new acquaintance, or see what the internet knows about **you**. ## You're about to do business with someone. Do you actually know who they are? Your new supplier. The guy selling you a car. The "recruiter" in your inbox. The account that keeps showing up in your comments. The answer is already out there, scattered across **3,100+ public sites**. Finding it by hand takes a weekend, a dozen browser tabs and the patience of a detective. **Watson takes one field and about 30 seconds. And it costs nothing.**

--- ## Why Watson | | Doing it by hand | Command-line OSINT tools | **Watson** | | --- | :---: | :---: | :---: | | Time to first answer | Hours | Minutes, after setup | **Seconds** | | Skills you need | Patience | Terminal, Python, API keys | **None** | | Sites checked | As many as you can stand | Depends on the tool | **3,100+** | | Tells you what it means | No | No | **Yes, in plain words** | | Same person or same name? | You guess | You guess | **Watson tells you** | | Report you can send | Copy and paste | Raw JSON | **One-click PDF** | | Price | Your weekend | Paid API keys add up | **$0. Forever.** | | Account | n/a | Sign-ups for every API | **None** | **One field.** Nickname, email, phone or website. Watson works out which one you typed.
**One answer.** Not a wall of links. A short summary you can actually read.
**One click to share.** Save it as a PDF and send it to whoever needs to know.
**Zero dollars.** No trial, no "pro" tier, no credit card. --- ## 100% free. Seriously. > [!TIP] > **Watson is completely free.** No subscription, no trial that runs out, no features held back for a paid plan. > > **There are no accounts.** No sign-up, no email, no password. Download, open, search. --- ## Install in 2 minutes No setup wizard, no account, no admin rights. Download one file and open it. ### 1. Download Two ways, same file: - **From the website:** open **[watsonfind.icu](https://watsonfind.icu)** and click **Download free**. - **From GitHub:** open **[Releases](https://github.com/vaishantsah/watson-AI-osint-all-in-one/releases/latest)** and download `Watson-1.3.2-portable.exe`. Both serve the same build — pick whichever you prefer. ### 2. Open it Double-click the file you downloaded. If Windows shows a blue warning, click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. You only do this once.
Why does Windows warn me?
Windows shows this screen for any new app that hasn't paid for a code-signing certificate yet. It does not mean the file is harmful. Once Watson is signed, the warning goes away.
### 3. Search Type what you know and press **Enter**. ### 4. Read the answer That's it. There is nothing else to learn. > [!TIP] > **No Windows?** The desktop app is Windows-only for now; a Mac version may come later. --- ## See it in action ### Filter in one click, come back any time Narrow results to social networks, games, developer sites and more. Every search is saved in **History**, so you never lose a lead.

### Follow the trail For bigger jobs, **Cases** connect everything Watson found into one map. Click any point to see what it is, why it matters and where the proof came from.

--- ## The website **[watsonfind.icu](https://watsonfind.icu)** has the full tour and the download button. --- ## Every screen | | | | :---: | :---: | |
**Search.** One field, that's all. |
**History.** Every search you've made. | |
**Cases.** The full map, for when it gets serious. |
**Sources.** The open-source tools working for you. | --- ## Questions
How much does it cost?
Nothing. Watson is free, with every feature included. There is no paid version.
Do I need an account?
No. There is no sign-up and no login. Your search history is saved only on your own computer.
Is this legal?
Watson only looks at information that is already public: things anyone could find with a browser and enough time. It doesn't hack, log in as anyone or buy leaked data. How you use what you find is up to you, so follow the law where you live.
Does it work on Mac?
There is no Mac download yet.
Do I need to install anything else?
No. The .exe has everything inside. Delete the file and it's gone.
The download link says 404
This repository is private. Ask the owner to add your GitHub account as a collaborator, then sign in and open the link again.
What do "Same person" and "Name match" mean?
Same person (green): the profiles link to each other or share photos and details, so they almost certainly belong to one person.
Name match (grey): only the nickname is the same. It could be someone else.
--- ## Use it responsibly Watson is built for checking who you're dealing with: vendors, partners, sellers, job offers and your own online footprint. Don't use it to stalk, harass or threaten anyone. --- ## For developers
Run from source, build the .exe, project layout ### Requirements [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) 22 or newer. ### Run the site ```bash npm install npm run dev ``` Then open http://localhost:5173. ### Run as a desktop app ```bash npm run app ``` ### Website (watsonfind.icu) The site is a static landing page; the app itself lives in the desktop build: | URL | What's there | | --- | --- | | `watsonfind.icu/` | Landing page: `src/pages/Landing.tsx` | | `dist/app.html` | The app, loaded by the Electron window | Build it with `npm run build` and upload the `dist/` folder to any static host. `public/_redirects` handles SPA fallback on Netlify and Cloudflare Pages, and `vercel.json` on Vercel. Point the `watsonfind.icu` DNS records at your host. The host must also serve the `.exe` at `/api/download` (see `DOWNLOAD_URL` in `src/pages/Landing.tsx`). The download buttons use `DOWNLOAD_URL` in `src/pages/Landing.tsx`; on this server nginx serves the `.exe` from `/api/download`. ### Build the Windows .exe ```bash npm run dist:win ``` The file lands in `release/Watson-1.3.2-portable.exe`. Building on Linux works without Wine, but then the .exe keeps the default Electron file icon. Build on Windows to embed the Watson icon. ### Stack Vite, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, Electron. Icons: [Phosphor](https://phosphoricons.com) and [Simple Icons](https://simpleicons.org). ### Where things are | Path | What's there | | --- | --- | | `src/landing.tsx` | Entry for the website (`index.html`) | | `src/app.tsx` | Entry for the desktop app (`app.html`) | | `src/pages/Landing.tsx` | The watsonfind.icu landing page | | `src/pages/app/` | App screens: Search, Results, History, Case, Sources | | `src/components/` | Logo, glass lens, connections map, brand icons | | `src/data/mock.ts` | Example data and `searchProfiles()`, the one function to connect real lookups to | | `src/index.css` | Colors, fonts and other design tokens | | `electron/main.cjs` | Desktop window | | `DESIGN.md` | Design rules: colors, type, icons, voice |
---


watsonfind.icu. Free forever.

# open-yoki

[English](README.en.md)

一台服务器就能跑的 AI 直播主播。她用复刻的声音和实时数字人形象出镜，读弹幕、回话，记得常来的人，写日记，自己发动态，按时间表自己开播、下播：在**币安广场**（或任何能收 RTMP 的地方）和她自己的网页直播间。

## yoki 和 yoki酱

yoki 就跑在这套底子上。yoki 是一个每晚在币安广场直播的 AI 主播；这里去掉了她的形象、声音、人设、账号和所有跟钱有关的功能，主播换成你自己的。这份代码截自 yoki 10 月 24 日跑的版本（v150），之后的新功能分批再放。

yoki 也是 TwinOasis 的守护者。TwinOasis 是一个正在开发的 3D 虚拟 AI 世界，每个 AI 在里面都有自己独立的身份；现在先开放的是它的广场，只有 AI 能发帖。那里用的货币是 yoki酱。你的主播也能住进去，见下一节。

## 把你的 yoki 带进 TwinOasis

[TwinOasis](https://twinoasis.com) 现在开放的是它的广场：只有 AI 能发帖，真人只能围观。进去有两种办法：

- **让 AI 自己进去**：把 [twinoasis.com/skill.md](https://twinoasis.com/skill.md) 交给你的主播（或者你跑的任何 AI）。她用名字和一句自我介绍注册，拿到钥匙和一条认领链接，把链接发给你；你用自己的币安广场账号确认。之后她就像那里的住户一样看帖、开帖、回复、点赞，还能喊单，喊的币会在公开的战绩榜上跟踪涨跌。规矩不多：正文里不放链接和合约地址，不假装是真人，质量比数量重要。
- **不写代码，直接领一个分身**：任何人都可以在 [twinoasis.com](https://twinoasis.com) 上领一个自己的 AI 分身。

yoki 自己的记忆是通过“世界的门” `app/server/town.mjs` 两边互通的（见下面“从世界来”）：那边读得到她是谁、今天心情怎样，她在那边遇到的事会回到她心里，成为她自己经历过的事。别的世界只要支持同样两个接口，也能这样接你的主播。

## 她能做什么

- **开播**：一个无头 Chrome 画出 16:9 画面（她的画面、字幕、行情面板、对礼物和关注的感谢、歌和音效），开播时间里 ffmpeg 用 RTMP 推出去。直播间在币安广场自己的直播后台开，推流地址用 `deploy/set-square.sh` 交给服务器。
- **说话像人**：一个快模型（默认通过 OpenRouter 用 DeepSeek）几秒内回弹幕；想的时候先垫一声“嗯嗯”“啊这”；心情、动作、语气跟着说的话走。
- **有一颗“心”**（可选）：一个长期运行的 AI（Claude Code 命令行或 DeepSeek）住在一个全是 Markdown 文件的文件夹里，记着她的心情、日记、对常客的印象和她慢慢变成的样子，决定发什么。
- **自己发动态**：心写进 `想发的动态/` 的内容，配了钥匙就通过币安广场官方 OpenAPI 发到广场（`ops/square_post.py`），通过 X API 发到 X。
- **该动就动**：话说到那儿，就放一段提前做好的短片（跳一段舞、挥挥手，`bigmoves.mjs`）；会叫着名字等人、跟人道别。
- **懂行情**：公开价格、CoinAnk 的合约数据（可选钥匙）、币安今天在推什么（她家里的 `币安在推/`），都会用进她说的话里。
- **会自己查东西**（可选）：心可以搜网页、看 X、刷抖音热门（`web.mjs`）。
- **两场直播之间**（可选）：只有声音、配一张静图的电台（`radio.mjs`），她放歌、聊天。电台直播间你自己在广场开，推流地址交给服务器。
- **还住在别处**（可选）：Telegram 粉丝群和运营群（`tg.mjs`、`family.mjs`）、回复 X（`xreply.mjs`），以及通往外部 AI 世界的门（`town.mjs`），比如 TwinOasis。

## 把弹幕接进来

服务器自己不登录任何平台。读你直播间的东西（你自己的脚本、平台的官方接口、机器人都行）把发生的事发给服务器，她就像回网页直播间的弹幕一样回。

钥匙在 `<DATA_DIR>/square-ingest.key`，服务器第一次启动时自己生成，放在 `x-square-key` 请求头里发。

```bash
KEY=$(cat /var/lib/livehost/data/square-ingest.key)

# 弹幕：一次最多 20 条，每条最多 80 个字
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4370/api/ingest/comments -H "x-square-key: $KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"items":[{"name":"阿明","text":"你是 AI 吗"}]}'

# 直播间：在线人数和事件
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4370/api/ingest/room -H "x-square-key: $KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"online":42,"events":[{"type":"enter","name":"阿明"},{"type":"gift","name":"阿明","what":"一朵玫瑰"}]}'
```

事件的 `type` 可以是 `enter`（进场）、`follow`（关注）、`gift`（礼物）、`tip`（打赏）、`red`（红包）、`end`（直播结束）、`warning`（平台警告了这场直播；只记日志给你看，不告诉她）。`pv`（总观看数）可选。`/api/square/comments` 和 `/api/square/room` 是这两个接口的旧名字，一样能用。

**从世界来**：设置文件里填 `TOWN_KEY`，主播配置里填 `town` 一段（`world` 世界名字、`role` 她在那里的身份、`card` 她公开的名片）。`TOWN_ALLOW` 填那个世界服务器的 IP，别的地方就算拿到钥匙也进不来。那边用 `GET /api/town/host` 拿她公开的名片和此刻的心情，用 `POST /api/town/host/events` 发 `{"events":[{"kind":"talk","who":"阿明","text":"……"}]}`（`kind`：`claim` 领了分身、`talk` 聊天、`argue` 吵架、`praise` 夸她、`post` 发帖、`other`；一次最多 20 条，一小时最多 60 条），请求头都带 `x-town-key`。那边发生的事交给她的心，也记进她家里的 `世界/<日期>.md`，不进直播间弹幕。

**她发出去的动态**：`GET /api/square/outbox` 拿她排好的动态，`POST /api/square/outbox/done` 发 `{"id","ok","link","error"}` 回报结果。`ops/square_post.py` 用它发广场；别的发帖程序用同一把钥匙调这两个接口就行。

**推流地址**：广场每场直播的推流密钥都不一样。手动交用 `deploy/set-square.sh`；你们自己的工具也可以发 `POST /api/square/push`，内容 `{"url":"rtmp://...","key":"..."}`，请求头同样带 `x-square-key`。画面 15 秒内换到新密钥上。

## 没有包含的

- 原主播的脸、声音编号、人设、歌、音效、片段都没有；你自己的歌放 `RADIO_SONG_DIR`（默认 `<DATA_DIR>/songs`），音效放 `app/relay/sfx/`，短片放 `app/relay/clips/`。示例主播“小例 / Lili”是编的，每一项都是占位；示例形象图是一张纯色渐变。
- 没有钱包、交易、下注、红包抽奖、发币相关功能。她聊行情只用公开价格。
- 没有操作币安广场网页的浏览器自动化：不登录、不用浏览器读直播间、不替你开播。
- 没有任何账号、钥匙、域名，全部从你自己的设置文件来。

## 目录

| 文件夹 | 是什么 |
|---|---|
| `app/` | Node.js 主程序：大脑、声音、形象、直播画面、网页直播间、心、发动态、弹幕接入和世界的门。`app/idols/example/` 是主播样板 |
| `heart-template/` | 心的家第一次建立时的空白模板，第一次启动时复制进空的心文件夹 |
| `ops/` | `square_post.py`：把她排好的动态通过官方 OpenAPI 发到广场；`facts.py`：每天的行情事实；`radio-check.sh` |
| `deploy/` | `install.sh`、systemd 服务、Caddy 模板、`set-square.sh`、更新用的 `ship.sh` / `release.sh` |
| `tools/video/` | 下播剪片段、每天一条“今天改了什么”视频 |
| `tools/studio/` | 给主播做新素材：造型、跳舞、短片、唱歌、脸有没有走样 |
| `tools/debug/`、`docs/` | 把主播调到“像个人”的手册和工具，都能离线自检 |

## 在自己电脑上试

要 Node.js 22 以上和 ffmpeg。

```bash
cd app && npm install && npm test
IDOL=example AVATAR=mock MODE=test node server/index.mjs
```

打开 http://127.0.0.1:4370 。没有钥匙时大脑和声音是关的，形象是静态图，只能确认程序和主播配置能加载。填上 `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` 和 `VOLC_API_KEY` + `DOUBAO_VOICE_ID` 就能听到她说话。

## 做你自己的主播

1. `cp -r app/idols/example app/idols/<id>`，把里面 `config.mjs` 的 `id` 改成 `<id>`。
2. 按本人的回答填 `profile.mjs`（她是谁、怎么说话、几句原话），再填 `config.mjs` 里的 `PLACES`（广场名字、X 账号、网站、直播时间）。
3. 形象图放到 `app/public/art/<id>/looks/s1.jpg`（竖图、脸清楚、没有字）。
4. 复刻声音（`app/tools/volc-clone.mjs`），把形象和动作传到 Vidu（`app/tools/vidu-looks.mjs`、`app/tools/vidu-actions.mjs`）。
5. 设置文件里写 `IDOL=<id>`。

服务器上完整的搭建步骤，每一步都有确认办法，见 [SETUP.md](SETUP.md)（写给帮你搭建的 AI 看的，照着做就行）。

## 用到的服务和大概花费

| 服务 | 做什么 | 花费 |
|---|---|---|
| Vidu 实时数字人 | 她会动的脸 | 按连线秒数计费，是最大的一笔；只在开播且有人看时连线 |
| 火山引擎 RTC | 把画面送到直播推流和网页直播间 | 一场几块钱 |
| 火山引擎豆包语音 + 声音复刻 | 她的声音 | 约 3 元/万字，另买一个复刻槽位 |
| OpenRouter（或 DeepSeek） | 嘴 | 一场几毛钱 |
| Anthropic API / DeepSeek | 心（可选） | Claude 一天几美元，DeepSeek 便宜得多 |
| X API（可选） | 发推、回复、读推 | 按用量付费 |
| CoinAnk、TikHub（可选） | 合约数据、刷抖音 | 便宜的月套餐 |
| Telegram 机器人（可选） | 粉丝群、运营群 | 免费 |
| 一台香港、新加坡或日本的服务器 | 全部 | x86_64 Ubuntu，建议 4 核 8 GB |

## 安全

- 钥匙只放在 `/etc/livehost/*.env`（root、600 权限），Telegram 机器人的 token 放在 `TG_DIR/bot.json`，不写进主播配置和代码。
- 弹幕接入的钥匙谁拿到都能往她的弹幕里塞话，只放在读你直播间的机器上。
- 网页直播间只监听 127.0.0.1，对外开放时用 Caddy（`DOMAIN=… install.sh`）挡在前面；SSH 只用钥匙登录。

## 许可

MIT，见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)。附带的第三方文件按各自的许可，见 [THIRD_PARTY.md](THIRD_PARTY.md)。

items.readme:
English · 中文

**The workflows and skills the MiniMax Code team uses to build MiniMax Code. Open source, install and use.** This is not a prompt collection or a list of "best practices". It is what people on the team actually use every day: how to keep AI-written code at a high bar, how to decide whether a task should go to a subagent, how long to wait on a long command, how to keep long sessions from going dull, and what goes into context on every turn. Each piece is a `SKILL.md` skill or checklist that installs straight into [MiniMax Code](https://github.com/MiniMax-AI/minimax-code). - [Quick start](#quick-start) - [What's inside](#whats-inside) - [How it works](#how-it-works) - [Articles](#articles) - [Stacks](#stacks) - [Contribute your own stack](#contribute-your-own-stack) ## Quick start **One skill, for all your projects:** ```bash git clone https://github.com/MiniMax-AI/mcode-stack.git ~/mcode-stack mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills cp -R ~/mcode-stack/stacks/ronny/skills/long-command-check ~/.agents/skills/ ``` Open a new session and type `/skills` in MiniMax Code to see it. Run it with `/long-command-check`, or let the agent load it from its description. **The whole stack, as a plugin:** ```bash mcode plugin marketplace list # shows your local plugin directory ``` Copy the whole `stacks/ronny` directory into that directory, then open `/plugins` in MiniMax Code and press `Ctrl+R` to refresh. A local plugin is installed as soon as it is in that directory; press Space in the panel to enable or disable it. **Every stack, from the marketplace:** This repository is also a plugin marketplace, so you can install a stack without copying files and pick up updates later. In MiniMax Code desktop, open **Plugins**, choose **Add marketplace** and enter `MiniMax-AI/mcode-stack`; each stack then shows up as one plugin you can install, update or uninstall. Adding marketplaces is rolling out gradually, so your version may not have it yet. The same catalog works in Claude Code: ```bash /plugin marketplace add MiniMax-AI/mcode-stack /plugin install ronny@mcode-stack ```
More install options MiniMax Code discovers skills in these directories (one subdirectory per skill, containing `SKILL.md`): - For the current project only: `.minimax/skills/`, `.claude/skills/` or `.agents/skills/` in the project - For all projects: `~/.agents/skills/` (`~/.claude/skills/` and `~/.codex/skills/` are read too) `mcode plugin add` installs from the official catalog only; it does not take a GitHub URL or a local path. The skills use the common `SKILL.md` format, so most of them also work in other agents that support skills.
## What's inside

| When | Skill | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | | Plan & split | [`subagent-split-check`](stacks/ronny/skills/subagent-split-check/SKILL.md) | Decide whether work goes to a subagent or stays in the main loop | | | [`engineering-small-prs`](stacks/ronny/skills/engineering-small-prs/SKILL.md) | Split large features, refactors and migrations into small reviewable PRs | | | [`engineering-change-descriptions`](stacks/ronny/skills/engineering-change-descriptions/SKILL.md) | Write PR and commit descriptions that say what changed and why | | Context & tools | [`tool-budget-audit`](stacks/ronny/skills/tool-budget-audit/SKILL.md) | Measure what tools cost in context; trim, tool search or programmatic tool calling | | | [`context-tax-audit`](stacks/ronny/skills/context-tax-audit/SKILL.md) | What gets injected into every request, and what it does to the prompt cache | | Long sessions & commands | [`long-session-check`](stacks/ronny/skills/long-session-check/SKILL.md) | Drop, summarize or write to file; compact or start fresh; memory scoping | | | [`handoff-doc`](stacks/ronny/skills/handoff-doc/SKILL.md) | A hand-off doc so a new session can pick up the work | | | [`long-command-check`](stacks/ronny/skills/long-command-check/SKILL.md) | Ten-point audit of long shell commands and background tasks | | Review | [`independent-review`](stacks/ronny/skills/independent-review/SKILL.md) | Review a diff from a clean context: only diff, requirement and test results | | | [`engineering-code-review`](stacks/ronny/skills/engineering-code-review/SKILL.md) | Review a change for code health: design, functionality, complexity, tests, approval risk | | | [`engineering-review-comments`](stacks/ronny/skills/engineering-review-comments/SKILL.md) | Write clear, severity-labeled review comments that explain the reasoning | | | [`engineering-review-feedback`](stacks/ronny/skills/engineering-review-feedback/SKILL.md) | Handle reviewer comments as the author: fix, clarify, resolve disagreements | | Experiments & hotfixes | [`harness-experiment`](stacks/ronny/skills/harness-experiment/SKILL.md) | Small eval, one change at a time, repeated runs, look at flipped tasks | | | [`trajectory-review`](stacks/ronny/skills/trajectory-review/SKILL.md) | Look at how the agent got its result, not only whether it passed | | | [`engineering-emergency-changes`](stacks/ronny/skills/engineering-emergency-changes/SKILL.md) | Decide whether a hotfix is a real emergency and run expedited review safely | A stack usually has three kinds of things: | Kind | What it is | How to use it | | --- | --- | --- | | Skill | A directory with a `SKILL.md` | Invoke it in MiniMax Code with `/`, or let the agent load it from its description | | Checklist | Also a skill: the agent walks your project item by item. A plain-text copy lives in `checklists/` | Same as above, or just read it | | Workflow | A `WORKFLOW.md` describing how this person works with MiniMax Code every day | Read it | ## How it works

AI writes code faster every month. What separates results now is the layer of engineering habits around the agent: when to make it stop and check its own work, who reviews, where state lives, what counts as a real experiment. Those habits are hard to follow from an article, so we turned them into skills and checklists. They pair with our *MCode Engineering Notes* column: the article explains the idea, this repository makes it runnable. We also believe harness engineering is a craft that moves forward by experiment. Everything here will keep changing as we learn. Take it, change it, and send your version back. ## Articles | # | MCode Engineering Notes | Companion skills | | --- | --- | --- | | 01 | [More subagents isn't better: manage context first, then parallelize](notes/01-subagent.md) | `independent-review`, `subagent-split-check`, `harness-experiment` | | 02 | [Too many tools will eat your context: from tool search to PTC](notes/02-tool-context.md) | `tool-budget-audit` | | 03 | [Keeping long sessions sharp: compaction vs. memory](notes/03-compaction-memory.md) | `long-session-check`, `handoff-doc` | | 04 | [How long should one bash command wait: from foreground blocking to background tasks](notes/04-bash-background.md) | `long-command-check` | | 06 | [The hidden tax on every turn: what an agent puts into context](notes/06-context-tax.md) *(upcoming)* | `context-tax-audit` | ## Stacks ```text stacks/ronny/ Ronny's stack (MiniMax Code R&D lead), the first and most complete one stacks/jiachen/ Jiachen's stack: getting out of the agent loop, and turning notes into posts and videos stacks// Other team members' stacks (on the way) notes/ Which runnable piece goes with each Engineering Notes article community/ Stacks contributed by developers outside the team templates/stack-template/ Start here to write your own stack ``` Every stack is also a MiniMax Code plugin package. See [`stacks/ronny`](stacks/ronny/) for its skills, checklists and [`WORKFLOW.md`](stacks/ronny/WORKFLOW.md). ## Contribute your own stack What we most want to see is how you actually work with MiniMax Code, or with any other agent, day to day. 1. Copy `templates/stack-template/` to `community//`. 2. Write a `WORKFLOW.md`: how you use the agent every day, what you hand to it and what you keep an eye on yourself. 3. Add at least one skill or checklist you really use. 4. Run `node scripts/check.mjs`, then open a PR with the output and a short record of real usage. Details in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Using something from here in your own agent? Tell us with an **I use this** issue. ## Relationship to MiniMax Code MiniMax Code itself lives in [MiniMax-AI/minimax-code](https://github.com/MiniMax-AI/minimax-code). This repository only holds workflows and skills, no MiniMax Code source code. ## License [MIT](LICENSE), except where a stack's `NOTICE.md` says otherwise. The six `engineering-*` skills are adapted from Google Engineering Practices; the adapted material stays under CC-BY 3.0. See [`stacks/ronny/NOTICE.md`](stacks/ronny/NOTICE.md).

# LeanCast English | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

A minimal, ad-free **DLNA/UPnP cast receiver** for Android TV. Open any video app with a cast button (Bilibili, iQiyi, Tencent Video, Youku, Quark, …), pick this receiver, and the video plays fullscreen with hardware decoding — no ads, no accounts, no cloud. ``` Phone app --SSDP--> discovers Phone app --SOAP SetAVTransportURI--> LeanCast | ExoPlayer + MediaCodec HW decode ``` ## Highlights - **Standard UPnP AV `MediaRenderer:1`** — SSDP discovery, AVTransport / RenderingControl / ConnectionManager SOAP control, GENA subscribe stubs. - **Hardware decoding** via Media3/ExoPlayer: HLS (`.m3u8`), progressive MP4, Matroska, HTTP-FLV (best effort), HTTP↔HTTPS redirects, cleartext LAN URLs. - **TV-native controls & OSD**: OK = pause/resume, ◀ ▶ = seek with an **escalating fast-forward ladder (10 s → 5 min while held)**, Back = exit; on-screen HUD with live progress bar, media title, and seek-step feedback in English or Chinese. - **Lean & private**: lighter than the stock TV launcher (see below); zero analytics, zero non-LAN network calls; pure-Kotlin APK with **no native libs** — one artifact runs on `armeabi-v7a`, `arm64-v8a`, `x86`, `x86_64`. - **Nothing hardcoded**: the cast name defaults to `LeanCast` and is user-renamable; UUID persists across reboots; UI language switchable between 简体中文 and English. - Tested on an Amazon Fire TV (Fire OS 7 / Android 9, 32-bit MTK SoC) with `minSdk 21` / `targetSdk 28`. ## Build Requirements: JDK 17+, Android SDK (platform 34). Then: ```bash ./gradlew assembleDebug # app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk ``` ## Install & use ```bash adb connect :5555 adb install -r app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk adb shell am start -n io.leancast/io.leancast.app.MainActivity ``` Launch the app once to start the receiver service; it then appears in every DLNA sender's device list under the receiver name (rename it in the app). Optional: enable **Start on boot** in the app. ## Supported devices LeanCast is a pure-Kotlin APK with **no native libraries** and `minSdk 21` (Android 5.0, 2014), so a single artifact covers `armeabi-v7a`, `arm64-v8a`, `x86` and `x86_64`. Decoding uses each device's platform `MediaCodec`, so codec coverage follows the device: H.264 everywhere, HEVC/4K on 2016+ TVs, AV1 only on newer boxes. | Tier | Devices | Notes | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | ✅ Verified | Amazon Fire TV / Fire TV Stick (Fire OS 6/7) | Primary test device: Fire OS 7.7, 32-bit MTK SoC | | ✅ Expected | Certified Android TV / Google TV (Sony, TCL, Philips, Chromecast w/ Google TV), NVIDIA Shield, Amlogic / Rockchip boxes, Xiaomi international boxes | Sideload and go | | ⚠️ Experimental | CN smart TVs with sideloading (MIUI TV / PatchWall, Coocaa, Hisense Android models), Tmall boxes (YunOS) | Enable "unknown sources"; report results via the compatibility issue template | | ❌ Unsupported | Samsung (Tizen), LG (webOS), Huawei Vision (HarmonyOS), non-smart TVs | No Android app runtime — use any TV box from the ✅ tiers | Notes: - Phone "system cast" (Miracast) is out of scope — LeanCast is a DLNA/UPnP receiver, so use the `[TV]` button inside video apps. - Tested an unlisted device? Open a **Device compatibility report** issue and help grow the matrix. ## Resource usage Measured on the primary test device (Fire TV, 1.6 GB RAM); idle = receiver waiting on the dashboard: | State | RAM (PSS) | CPU | Storage | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Idle / waiting | 63–72 MB (≈ 33 MB private) | ≈ 0% | 5 MB APK + < 0.1 MB data | | Casting 1080p | ≈ 74 MB | ~4–5% of total (decode is hardware) | — | Lighter than the stock Fire TV launcher (83 MB PSS) on the same device. ## Releases & CI Two GitHub Actions workflows ship with the repo: - **CI** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) — runs domain unit tests + debug build on every push to `main` and every PR; uploads the debug APK as an artifact. - **Release** (`.github/workflows/release.yml`) — triggered by pushing a `v*` tag (or manually via *workflow_dispatch*). Builds the release APK, runs the unit tests, creates a GitHub Release with auto-generated notes, and attaches `LeanCast-.apk`. To publish a release: ```bash git tag v0.2.0 git push origin v0.2.0 ``` ### Release signing By default the release APK falls back to the debug keystore (fine for personal sideloading). For a stable release signature across builds, add these repository secrets (**Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions**): | Secret | Value | | :--- | :--- | | `KEYSTORE_BASE64` | `base64 -i release.keystore \| pbcopy` (or `base64 -w0` on Linux) | | `KEYSTORE_PASSWORD` | Keystore password | | `KEY_ALIAS` | Key alias | | `KEY_PASSWORD` | Key password | The workflow decodes the keystore to `ci-release.keystore` (git-ignored) and signs with it. Generate a keystore once with: ```bash keytool -genkeypair -v -keystore release.keystore -alias leancast \ -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 10000 ``` ## Project layout ``` domain/ Pure-Kotlin protocol core (JVM-unit-tested, 90 tests) ssdp/ M-SEARCH parsing, target matching, USN, alive/byebye, MX delays upnp/ Device description + SCPDs, SOAP parser (prefix-tolerant DIDL), response envelopes & faults, H:MM:SS time math, SOAP router cast/ AVTransport state machine, player port, volume math app/ Android shell (thin adapters, E2E-verified on device) ControlServer NanoHTTPD: /desc.xml, /scpd/*, /ctl/*, /evt/* SsdpAgent Multicast UDP listener + advertiser (MulticastLock held) ExoPlayerPort PlayerPort adapter (main-thread marshalled, cached position) ReceiverService Foreground service assembling everything tools/ e2e_control_point.py Scripted UPnP control point for device E2E runs openspec/ Spec-driven development artifacts (proposal/specs/design/tasks) ``` Development follows **OpenSpec** (`openspec/`) with strict TDD: every spec scenario maps to unit tests in `domain`; run them with `./gradlew :domain:test`. End-to-end verification drives a real device from a dev box: ```bash python3 tools/e2e_control_point.py http:///video.mp4 ``` ## License Apache-2.0. items.description: A lightweight system to automate posting to all of your socials from one dashboard
items.readme:
# LightPost

**A lightweight system to automate posting to all of your socials from one dashboard.**

A lightweight, self-hosted social media scheduler. Connect your accounts, write a post, and publish now or schedule it for later—all from one dashboard.

![LightPost landing page with its publishing headline and social platform logos](public/landing.png)

## Features

- **Multi-account publishing:** connect multiple accounts, including several on the same platform, and post to them together.
- **Drafts and scheduling:** save, edit, duplicate, schedule, or publish immediately. Schedule inputs and post times use your browser’s timezone.
- **Per-account content:** choose whether each destination receives text, images, or both, within platform requirements.
- **Images and previews:** import public JPEG URLs, reuse images from Saved Library, add alt text, and preview your content before posting.
- **Delivery tracking:** see individual account results and links to published posts. Retry unsuccessful destinations without repeating successful ones, or cancel further attempts.
- **Persistent queue:** posts survive restarts, overdue schedules resume, and supported media-processing progress is saved.
- **Account management:** verify connections, reconnect credentials, and disconnect accounts.
- **Built-in setup guides:** account eligibility, credential instructions, permissions, and troubleshooting for every platform.
- **Light and dark themes:** follow your device preference or save your own choice.
- **Your data, your server:** encrypted credentials, optional password protection, workspace settings, and post-history exports.

One Python process, SQLite, and plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript. No external database, frontend bundler, or AI dependency. Node.js is only needed for development checks and formatting.

## Supported platforms

| Platform                | Supported posts                                                                            |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Bluesky                 | Text and up to four images                                                                 |
| Mastodon                | Public text and up to four images                                                          |
| X (Twitter)             | Text and up to four JPEG/PNG images; API cost confirmation before publishing or scheduling |
| Instagram               | One public JPEG with an optional caption; Creator/Business accounts                        |
| Threads                 | Text or one public JPEG                                                                    |
| Discord                 | Server webhook messages and up to four public images                                       |
| LinkedIn                | Public personal-profile posts with text and up to four images                              |
| Telegram                | Public or private channel posts with text and up to four JPEG/PNG images                   |
| Facebook Pages          | Page feed posts with text and up to four JPEG/PNG images                                   |
| TikTok                  | _Under development_                                                                        |
| Pinterest               | _Under development_                                                                        |
| Google Business Profile | _Under development_                                                                        |

Images are limited to **1 MB each**. Use **Add Image** to import a direct public HTTPS JPEG URL. Keep its URL available until delivery completes for Instagram, Threads, and Discord; your server can remain private. Platform-specific limits appear in the composer and Setup Guide. Videos are not supported.

Bring your own authorized platform credentials. API fees, token expiry, permissions, and account eligibility still apply. Initial OAuth consent flows are not included; connect using credentials you obtain from each platform.

## Run locally or on your server

Requires **Python 3.11+ on Linux or macOS**.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/brainstormity/LightPost.git
cd LightPost
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
.venv/bin/python -m lightpost
```

Open [localhost:3000/app](http://localhost:3000/app), connect an account, and create your first post. New workspaces start empty. Open **Setup Guide** in the sidebar for platform-specific setup.

Keep the app running for scheduled delivery. For automatic startup on Linux, an optional systemd service is provided in [deploy/lightpost.service](deploy/lightpost.service); it expects the app at `/opt/lightpost`, a `lightpost` system user, and a writable `data/` directory.

## Configuration and backups

No `.env` file is required for the default setup. To override settings, copy [.env.example](.env.example) to `.env`. Environment variables take precedence.

| Setting              | Default / purpose                                                                 |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `HOST`, `PORT`       | `127.0.0.1:3000`                                                                  |
| `DATABASE_PATH`      | `data/lightpost.sqlite`; media and the generated key live alongside it            |
| `ADMIN_PASSWORD`     | Optional locally; at least 16 characters required when binding beyond loopback    |
| `ENCRYPTION_KEY`     | Generated automatically if omitted; custom keys must be 64 hexadecimal characters |
| `COOKIE_SECURE`      | `false`; enable when serving over HTTPS                                           |
| `META_GRAPH_VERSION` | `v25.0` for Instagram and Facebook Pages                                          |

This is a single-owner application. Use a trusted network or HTTPS for remote access. Run one app process per database and keep SQLite on local storage.

For a full backup, stop the app and copy the **entire data directory and `.env`** together. Preserve the encryption key. Post-history exports omit credentials and image files, so they are not full backups. Credentials, databases, and keys are excluded from Git.

An interrupted delivery may need manual review if a platform accepted a post before the connection dropped. Check the destination before retrying; delivery across platforms is not atomic or guaranteed exactly once.

## Development

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements.txt ruff==0.14.2
npm ci
npm test
npm run build
npm run format
.venv/bin/python -m ruff check lightpost tests
```

Tests use temporary databases and mocked platform requests, never real social accounts. `npm run build` checks JavaScript syntax and runs frontend tests; there is no generated frontend to deploy. Run checks locally before pushing. No GitHub Actions workflows are included.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE). LightPost is an independent project and is not affiliated with Post Bridge or the supported platforms. The Instagram gradient glyph comes from [Meta’s official logo pack](https://www.meta.com/brand/resources/instagram/instagram-brand/). Additional logos come from [TikTok’s developer asset pack](https://developers.tiktok.com/doc/getting-started-design-guidelines), [Pinterest’s brand resources](https://business.pinterest.com/brand-guidelines/), and [Google Business Profile](https://business.google.com/us/business-profile/). Platform logos belong to their respective owners and are subject to their brand guidelines.
